items.title: Who can be licensed as a physician? Not AI | American Medical Association
items.summary: The AMA is drawing a clear line between augmented intelligence (AI) as a tool to support healthcare and the practice of medicine. AI—often called artificial intelligence—can help doctors with clinical tasks, but it cannot be granted physician licensure, professional titles or certification to practice medicine, says new policy adopted at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting. [...] With this recent update to extensive, existing policy on AI, the AMA House of Delegates calls for AI-enabled technologies to be integrated into physician-led teams and used at the direction of the treating physician. AI tools used for clinical functions such as diagnosis, prescribing and care management should have transparent, auditable evidence demonstrating their safety and efficacy and be subject to appropriate regulation, documentation and liability requirements. [...] “AI can help physicians analyze information, identify patterns and support clinical decision-making, but patients deserve to know who is responsible for their care,” said AMA President Willie Underwood III, MD, MSc, MPH. “Physicians also need the authority, oversight and liability protections to make independent decisions when AI is part of the care team.”

items.title: Anthropic to raise $64bn in major stock market listing
items.summary:
This would value Anthropic at between $1.1 trillion and $1.3 trillion which, although large, is below the $2 trillion some analysts had predicted weeks ago.

It is floating at a volatile time for AI firms. After last week's US midterm elections, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns a Democrat-led Congress could slow development of AI and the buildout of data centres.

There are also wider fears over the billions of dollars being spent on AI and whether it will pay off. [...] Fiona Cincotta, a senior market analyst at City Index, said the amount Anthropic wants to raise is "fairly bullish" within "the volatility [and] concerns towards AI that we've seen in sort of particularly last week".

She told Reuters: "It's showing that they are still sort of upbeat about the outlook as far as AI is concerned and that obviously that they think that the demand is going to be there."

## Global stocks plunge as fears over US AI slowdown spread to Asia and Europe [...] # Anthropic to raise $64bn in major stock market listing

Getty Images Claude by Anthropic logo on a smartphone 

Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, is planning to raise up to $64bn (£48bn) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange.

The loss-making company said it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each in its initial public offering (IPO), which is expected to go ahead this month.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Apology May Be the Only Correct Use of AI - The Atlantic
items.summary:
People (me) are always saying about AI, “This is a solution looking for a problem!” and “Who would possibly want to delegate things like knowing information about your childrenor creating works of art to a third-party series of zeroes and ones?” But there are some things in life that nobody wants to do, such as get a root canal, amputate a limb, or deal with your cable provider. Or, perhaps, apologize simultaneously to your employees and your wife of 40 years for jeopardizing your business and [...] Now I am worried, based on Jensen Huang’s claim that this was “completely normal and not unusual” and an NVIDIA spokesperson’s insistence that his interactions with the alleged spy were “not unusual” that, actually, we’ll be seeing multiple emails like this. Finally, organic demand for AI! If so, the template will get better and better—that is, if we can still use the chips.

items.title: Hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp ứng dụng công nghệ, nâng cao sức cạnh tranh
items.summary: Tiến sĩ Chu Thúc Đạt, Phó Cục trưởng Cục Đổi mới sáng tạo (Bộ Khoa học và Công nghệ) cho biết, trong bối cảnh cạnh tranh ngày càng gay gắt, năng lực công nghệ có vai trò quan trọng, trực tiếp ảnh hưởng đến năng suất, chất lượng sản phẩm, hiệu quả sử dụng nguyên liệu và khả năng tham gia chuỗi giá trị của doanh nghiệp ngành chế biến, chế tạo. Trên cơ sở Chương trình phối hợp giai đoạn 2026 - 2030 với định hướng thúc đẩy khoa học, công nghệ và đổi mới sáng tạo gắn với các chuỗi giá trị ngành hàng [...] Chia sẻ về thực tiễn ứng dụng công nghệ vào sản xuất, Phó Giám đốc Công ty Trách nhiệm hữu hạn Sản xuất thương mại Phước Thành IV  Huỳnh Hồng Thắm cho biết, công ty đang đề xuất tiếp cận công nghệ chế biến khoai lang tím nhằm đa dạng hóa đầu ra, gắn sản phẩm chế biến với nhu cầu thị trường và người tiêu dùng. Với nền tảng công nghệ sẵn có trong lĩnh vực chế biến, kinh doanh gạo, đóng gói bao bì, cùng kinh nghiệm cải tiến quy trình sản xuất, công ty có điều kiện tiếp nhận, ứng dụng công nghệ mới [...] giá trị ngành hàng chủ lực, hội thảo là dịp để cụ thể hóa các nội dung phối hợp thông qua việc xác định nhu cầu công nghệ của doanh nghiệp, kết nối với các giải pháp phù hợp và huy động nguồn lực hỗ trợ triển khai vào thực tiễn sản xuất.

items.title: Sở Khoa học và Công nghệ Hà Tĩnh hướng dẫn xét công nhận sáng kiến và đánh giá hiệu quả đề tài khoa học
items.summary: Theo hướng dẫn, các giải pháp được xem xét công nhận là sáng kiến bao gồm: giải pháp kỹ thuật, giải pháp quản lý, giải pháp tác nghiệp và giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật. Trong đó, giải pháp kỹ thuật có thể là sản phẩm, vật liệu, giống cy trồng, vật nuôi hoặc quy trình công nghệ; giải pháp quản lý là phương pháp tổ chức, điều hành công việc; giải pháp tác nghiệp là các phương pháp thực hiện nghiệp vụ chuyên môn; còn giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật là việc áp dụng các giải pháp kỹ thuật

items.title: Thúc đẩy ứng dụng công nghệ sinh học, tạo đột phá cho nông nghiệp Việt Nam
items.summary:
Riêng năm 2024, nhiều sản phẩm công nghệ sinh học mới được phê duyệt, trong đó có ngô TELA, chuối kháng bệnh héo rũ Panama chủng TR4, bạch đàn tăng năng suất, dạ yến thảo phát sáng và trầu bà hỗ trợ lọc không khí. Những ứng dụng này cho thấy phạm vi phát triển của công nghệ sinh học không còn giới hạn ở mục tiêu nng cao năng suất cy trồng mà đang mở rộng sang nhiều lĩnh vực khác. [...] Các đại biểu tham gia phát biểu tại tọa đàm "Thúc đẩy ứng dụng hiệu quả cy trồng công nghệ sinh học tại Việt Nam". (Ảnh: TÙNG ĐINH)

 

Tuy nhiên, trước yêu cầu đổi mới mô hình tăng trưởng nông nghiệp, việc thúc đẩy nghiên cứu, làm chủ và ứng dụng các công nghệ mới, nhất là công nghệ chỉnh sửa gen, vẫn đặt ra nhiều vấn đề cần giải quyết về năng lực khoa học, cơ chế quản lý và thương mại hóa kết quả nghiên cứu. [...] ### Công nghệ sinh học ngày càng mở rộng ứng dụng trên toàn cầu

Phát biểu khai mạc hội thảo, Tiến sĩ Nguyễn Văn Long, Vụ trưởng Khoa học và Công nghệ (Bộ Nông nghiệp và Môi trường), cho biết công nghệ sinh học và chỉnh sửa gen trên thế giới đã đạt nhiều thành tựu quan trọng, góp phần tạo ra các giống cy trồng có năng suất, chất lượng cao và khả năng thích ứng tốt hơn với điều kiện bất lợi.

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary:
Dexterity: Our robots can perform significantly more tasks with greater performance and dexterity — from using everyday tools to handling delicate, flexible objects.
 Reliability: During a real-world proof-of-concept on Mercedes-Benz production lines, our models helped Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid pick and pack automotive parts with a 96% success rate. This could enable robots to take on monotonous work, to enable technicians to focus on complex build tasks. [...] Robots struggle to adapt to new unpredictable environments, our Gemini Robotics models give Apollo the ability to think, reason over multiple steps, and take action adapting to changes. In this proof-of-concept, Apollo 2 autonomously performs automotive kitting: the repetitive, physically taxing task of sorting individual parts from bulk bins into organized trays in the exact order needed for each vehicle on the line. Offloading this monotonous prep work helps keep the assembly line moving, [...] With Gemini Robotics 2.5, we expanded the model capabilities in task breadth, performance, and complexity. We evaluated the model across 200 distinct tasks — such as serving food with tongs, tying a bow on a gift box, and pipetting a liquid. These tasks represent a step toward human-level dexterity by combining a number of skills, including advanced tool use, complex manipulation of deformables, and handling delicate objects with finesse.

items.title: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak" - Ars Technica
items.summary: DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate. [...] Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark. [...] Overall, Gemini Robotics 2.5 manages a 30 to 100 percent higher success rate compared to the last version. It’s also 20 to 30 percent faster. But that’s based on laboratory testing. Google partnered with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz to see how capable this AI is when faced with the uncertainty of the world outside robotics labs. The Gemini-powered Apollo 2 robots kitted automotive parts in a few European factories, reaching a 96 percent success rate.

items.title: Sacramento Startup Takes on Difficult Childbirth With Soft Robotics | Comstock's magazine
items.summary:
Stork Labs Medical, based in Sacramento and Santa Cruz, is an emerging biomedical startup developing the Pelican device: a flexible, sensor-guided soft robotics tool created to make assisted vaginal deliveries safer and reduce emergency C-sections. The device is designed to spread force more evenly across the baby’s head to help prevent injury and give doctors real-time guidance with integrated sensors, says Maryam Tebyani, the company’s co-founder and CEO. [...] In a soft robotics lab, where researchers create robots from flexible material, she met Breanna “Bre” Baltaxe-Admony, the company’s co-founder and COO, who specializes in human-centered design. In the past few years, they have spoken with hundreds of obstetricians, midwives, doulas, new moms and other stakeholders in emergency childbirth for input, “seeking out others when we don’t have the answers,” Baltaxe-Admony says. [...] “The Stork Labs technology has the potential to dramatically change the way stalled labor is approached in a clinical setting, potentially leading to fewer emergency C-sections, and better outcomes for moms and babies,” Alexander says. “Although the road ahead of the company is a long one, I am personally very excited to see how they are able to bring their proprietary technology to market, and what impact it can have.”

items.title: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google | TechCrunch
items.summary: In an effort to make ChatGPT an even better consumer discovery engine, OpenAI is launching a host of new features designed to help companies control how users interact with their businesses. [...] On Tuesday, the company rolled out a Business Hub that will serve as a place where companies can create business profiles that — in a feature that greatly resembles the kind of profiles that Google and other search engines already offer — allow enterprises to verify and update information about their products and services. The feature is currently in beta. [...] OpenAI previously tried to position ChatGPT as an e-commerce hub by which users could buy products directly. This effort — which used a commission fee system — was viewed as a potentially huge source of revenue and a way to make ChatGPT a more direct Amazon competitor. However, that project ultimately failed to take off and, in March, the company retired the effort, which had even included a “checkout cart” feature.

items.title: OpenAI wants to be Google - Fast Company
items.summary:
OpenAI needs to build analytics that show advertisers the consumer intent based on their prompts. I want to know which categories of intent my impressions ran against. I want to know whether those people were exploring, comparing, or ready to act, and which needs and product criteria drove that engagement. I want to know which kinds of sweater prompts turned into business and, just as important, which didn’t. Google’s advertisers have had some version of that map for two decades. It’s why [...] |

That comparison is where every sweater brand wants to be standing, and OpenAI has started selling the spot. Advertisers can buy on a CPM or CPC basis through OpenAI’s beta self-service Ads Manager, measure conversions with a pixel and Conversions API, and access campaign-level performance reporting. OpenAI is also testing Sponsored Agents, which let a user start a separate conversation with an advertiser after clicking an ad.

So the plumbing exists.

## A SEARCH-CALIBER AD PLATFORM [...] OpenAI already has the hard part down, the thing Google spent years teaching people to do. People are telling ChatGPT their goals, problems, preferences, objections, and purchase criteria in their own words. What it hasn’t built is the advertiser’s map of all that intent.

items.title: OpenAI gives brands free ChatGPT agents alongside paid ads
items.summary:
The implications extend beyond the accuracy of individual tools. OpenAI’s decision to share its own data could also shift the balance of power in the growing AI visibility industry. As Sonata Insights’ founder and chief analyst Debra Aho Williamson pointed out, the entire AI visibility (AEO/GEO) industry is built on third-party research (and some guesswork) about what helps a brand show up in an answer. [...] “The fact that OpenAI will now share insights itself will take some of the power away from the third-party companies,” she said. “But OpenAI isn’t going to share everything it knows, and ChatGPT is only one of several AI platforms, so demand for what the AI visibility companies offer will remain strong.”

Business Hub and agents are free for now but Shomair didn’t rule out a paid model in the future. [...] So, OpenAI has built two routes into the same conversation for brands, and only one of them costs money. One through ChatGPT’s organic recommendations, and the other via paid placements.

Shomair said early testing of sponsored agents had shown “promising results,” particularly in the depth of conversations between consumers and businesses.

“When a consumer chooses to engage more deeply with our business, there’s a high level of intent there,” he said.
